subject: Hybrid regional pricing proposal and cross-region commit clarification
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@cloudscale.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@cloudscale.com
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: RE: regional pricing questions for hosted API

Neha —

Thanks for the quick demo last week. We pulled together estimated monthly usage (attached) and have a few follow-ups on pricing and how commits work across regions. High level: 

- We expect ~85M tokens/month initially, ramping to ~180M over 6 months. Usage will be spread roughly 60% US, 30% EU, 10% APAC.
- We are evaluating a 12-month committed spend to get a lower per-token rate.

Questions:  
1) Can Redwood apply a single blended commit (one pool) across regions so we don't have to split commitments by region? If not, how do you recommend structuring commits to avoid over-committing in EU or APAC?
2) If region-specific differences exist, what are the typical uplifts for EU and APAC relative to US hosted API pricing?
3) Do discounts scale off gross token consumption or net after function/tool calls/structured output?

Also attaching a spreadsheet with projected monthly mix. Need to present a recommendation to our procurement on Friday.

Thanks —
Samir
Director, Platform Engineering
CloudScale

Attachment: CloudScale_Monthly_Usage_Estimate.xlsx (spreadsheet, 34KB)

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@cloudscale.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: regional pricing questions for hosted API

Samir —

Appreciate the detail and the spreadsheet, helped a lot. High-level answers up front, then a proposal: 

- Yes — we can support a single committed pool that’s pooled across regions (blended commit). That is our recommended approach for customers with cross-region traffic who want flexibility.
- If you prefer region-specific SLAs or data residency guarantees we can split commits by region; otherwise pooling reduces the risk of wasted commit.
- Typical regional uplifts we apply when customers want region-isolated capacity: EU +5% and APAC +10% vs the US base rate (this accounts for regional infra and run-rate differences). With a pooled commit we apply a blended calculation rather than per-region uplifts.
- Discounts scale off billable token consumption (generation tokens + any charged structured-output tokens). Retries and system-initiated tokens are excluded. We can show a worked example against your spreadsheet.

Proposal (for consideration):
- 12-month commit, 120M tokens/month initial (with monthly true-up): base per-token list $0.00080
- Committed discount tiers applied to pooled consumption: 10% @ 50M, 18% @ 150M, 25% @ 350M (these are blended thresholds)
- Given your mix and ramp, we’d propose an introductory blended discount of 15% on committed consumption for first 6 months, then the standard tiering thereafter.
- If you need region isolation (EU/APAC), we can add per-region uplift: +5% EU, +10% APAC, applied after discount. Alternatively, you accept the pooled model and we will provide a weighted blended rate monthly.

Next steps: if this aligns, I’ll loop in legal with a draft MSA and request procurement’s preferred billing/legal terms. Marissa, Vivek — any concerns on the proposed thresholds and uplift semantics?

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0192

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: regional pricing questions for hosted API

Looping in a couple quick notes: 

- The proposed blended thresholds look defensible from a cost standpoint but we should guard the top-tier (25% @ 350M) for multi-year or larger ARR deals; for a 12-month single-year commit with current ramp I’d be comfortable with the 18% tier as the ceiling unless legal asks for concessions.
- For EU VAT/withholding: legal/finance typically prefers explicit gross list rate with regional uplift rather than embedding VAT in the discount — helps invoice clarity.
- Suggest adding a 90-day ramp clause where true-up is monthly but we allow +/- 15% variance before penalties. This reduces procurement friction.

I can take point on commercial terms with Legal once Neha confirms procurement comfort.

—Marissa
Director, Commercial Operations

From: Samir Patel <samir.patel@cloudscale.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, procurement@cloudscale.com
Cc: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@cloudscale.com>
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 08:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: regional pricing questions for hosted API

Thanks Neha and team. A couple clarifying points from procurement and finance: 

- Procurement prefers a single pooled commit if the blended rate is transparent and we can see the monthly weighted calculation. Can you provide the monthly weighted blended-rate calc using our projected mix?
- We need the EU uplift and any VAT implications spelled out on the quote. For APAC we may have a separate tax treatment.
- We are okay with a 12-month commit. Can you confirm whether unused committed tokens roll forward within the contract year, or if they are forfeited?

Goal: provide a single-line commercial summary for our CFO by Friday (required for approval).

Samir

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@cloudscale.com>, procurement@cloudscale.com
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 May 2026 16:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: regional pricing questions for hosted API

Samir —

Thanks — attached is a short one-pager (sent inline) that answers the CFO-friendly bullets and a worked blended-rate example against the numbers in your spreadsheet. Summary below: 

1) Pooled commit model: YES, Redwood supports a single pooled commit across regions. We calculate a monthly weighted blended rate by multiplying region consumption by that region’s base rate (US base, EU +5%, APAC +10%), summing, then applying the committed discount. Example with your mix (60/30/10) and 120M committed tokens: blended pre-discount rate = (0.6*$0.00080) + (0.3*$0.00080*1.05) + (0.1*$0.00080*1.10) = $0.000824/month-weighted average. After a proposed 15% committed discount the effective rate = $0.0007004/token.

2) VAT/tax: We will show gross line items on the quote and invoices. VAT will be added as applicable for EU entities; uplift stays visible.

3) Unused tokens: We offer monthly true-up with a 90-day tolerance window. Within the contract year, unused committed tokens may be rolled forward up to one quarter (i.e., 3 months) provided annual consumption meets the committed average; otherwise forfeiture applies per the MSA. We can be explicit in the SOW.

4) Next steps: I will attach a draft commercial quote and an SOW addendum for the pooled commit model and 90-day ramp clause. Marissa will escalate any deviation to pricing ceilings. If procurement confirms they can accept the pooled blended method, I’ll ask Legal to publish the redline-ready MSA and route for signature.

Please let me know if you need the blended calculation as a table for the CFO or a single-line effective rate for the sign-off.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: Draft_MSA_redlines_v3.pdf (redline, 58KB)
